A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ST-BoN and contain readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, and appendices. Corresponding content can be matched despite substantial rewriting, revised experiments, and appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, memory and latency measurements, human evaluation, ablations, and case studies.

after.justification: v2 reports original empirical evaluations, including revised benchmark results, efficient-BoN comparisons, and a new comparison of CoE scoring with majority voting.

M1.justification: The early-divergence detection, CoE scoring, voting across the buffer window, and truncation procedure remain. However, v1 fixes the window length at 20 tokens, whereas v2 defines tau = mc and uses tau = c by default. This introduces an adaptive stopping rule within the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MATH, TheoremQA, GPQA, MMLU, revised CNNDM, and AlpacaFarm, covering the same reasoning, knowledge, summarization, and instruction-following tasks. Additional model configurations and larger sampling budgets do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated SBoN, CARDS, and TreeBoN comparisons on MATH and AlpacaFarm (Appendix B, Figure 9). The main reasoning reward model changes from Math-Shepherd-7B to Skywork, previously an appendix comparator. The reward-model ablation replaces Math-Shepherd with Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-7B while retaining Skywork and RLHFlow.

E3.justification: Sampling budgets extend to N = 80, versus maxima of 50 in v1's objective-task plots and 20 in its subjective-task plots. The large-model experiment changes from Llama3-70B to Qwen2.5-72B with a matched 72B verifier, and window ablations use multiples of c. v2 explicitly excludes reward-model loading from trade-off timing, although its latency discussion retains loading language. Its conflicting GPT-4o-Turbo and GPT-4-Turbo names leave any judge-model change unresolved.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused control testing CoE against majority voting after full generation (Appendix D.4, Table 2), and revises window sensitivity analysis around tau/c. Existing component-ablation questions, sampling-robustness analyses, and three case studies remain. Model-scaling and reward-model sensitivity studies are retained with revised model configurations.

E5.justification: v2 Section 5.1 first states that results are averaged over four evaluation runs; v1 supplies no run count. This is newly reported repetition information, not evidence that the number of runs increased. Neither version provides corresponding confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 revises numerous cost-performance curves and the computed memory-reduction results. The instruction-following finding changes from ST-BoN outperforming Full-BoN to reward-model Full-BoN performing better at equal N, with ST-BoN matching it through larger N. New results include efficient-BoN comparisons and Table 2: at N = 20 on MATH, CoE scores 73.1 versus majority voting's 72.7. Changed settings preclude treating these as controlled v1-to-v2 performance gains.

T1.justification: v1 motivates early consistency through a hypothesis and empirical validation. v2 adds Theorem 1, Lipschitz and bounded-increment assumptions, and a maximal-coupling/Markov-inequality proof in Section 3.1 and Appendix A. The memory-reduction derivation also changes to include the buffer window, replacing the E[c]/E[T] term with 2E[c]/E[T] under tau = c.

C1.justification: v2 introduces a claimed theoretical justification and explicitly claims that prior methods do not address both efficiency bottlenecks together. The abstract and conclusion emphasize cost-performance trade-offs rather than broadly comparable or superior performance. Claimed memory savings decrease from over 90% to over 80%, while the abstract specifies 70–80% computational savings at matched performance and 3–4 accuracy points at matched cost.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for adapting the window to c, reward models struggling with incomplete reasoning fragments, and CoE capturing process information beyond final-answer voting. Results are reinterpreted around increasing N to compensate for lower equal-N performance. A new societal-impact discussion asserts trustworthiness, no additional safety risks, and possible bias mitigation. The hidden-state-access and task-length limitations were already present in v1.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code/data repository statement and newly specifies three graduate-student annotators, 50 evaluation samples, averaging across annotators, and approximately 16 hours per annotator. These disclose details absent from v1 without establishing a changed human study. The checklist still answers No to open access with sufficient reproduction instructions, so the repository statement alone does not establish complete reproducibility.

R1.justification: v1's brief discussion of speculative rejection expands into detailed positioning against SBoN, CARDS, and TreeBoN, including Appendix B's comparison table and experiments. v2 also distinguishes sequential from parallel scaling and adds BoNBoN, BOND, and vBoN as training-time distillation approaches. This substantially revises the account of competing approaches and ST-BoN's claimed advantages.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method narrative, results discussion, and related work are extensively rewritten and reorganized. v2 separates theoretical support from the algorithm, organizes results as objective and subjective tasks, restructures related work, and reorganizes the appendices. Limitations move into the main document, alongside expanded societal-impact material and a conference checklist.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from two-column to single-column layout. Results are regrouped into model-specific figures, with Qwen results consolidated in the main text and other models moved to the appendix. Revised plots add equal-N connectors and cost-saving annotations; window-ablation axes change. Two new comparison tables are added, while the eight existing case-study tables are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: Including the previously omitted buffer-window memory cost, evaluating efficient-BoN competitors, and adding the full-generation CoE control strengthen the empirical case. However, v2 elevates theoretical support to a central claim while Appendix A uses maximal coupling and Section 2 specifies independent sampling; applicability of the assumptions to the squared-CoE measure is also unestablished. These empirical gains coexist with a material unresolved gap in the new theoretical justification, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
